$comment: Global sourcing registry for independent contest catalog construction. Every contest in the catalog must trace to a sponsor on this list, and a test enforces that. Organizations are grouped by tier: work top-down. `url_verified: true` means the URL itself was confirmed during research; the rest are the organization's known primary domain and should be confirmed on first use. READ `counts_are_estimates` BEFORE PLANNING A PASS.
sourcing_rule: NEVER populate a contest record from an aggregator. Only from the sponsoring organization's own published rules. If the sponsor's page cannot be found, the record stays unverified and does not ship.
counts_are_estimates: `estimated_total` on every org entry is a guess made before any of that sponsor's pages were read. It is NOT a target and it is NOT a denominator. Where a sponsor has actually been worked, verification has moved the number in both directions -- 10-10 was estimated at four QSO Parties and runs three; AGCW's ten includes one that publishes no closing time; NCJ's five dropped an SSB Sprint that no longer exists. `encoded` and `encoded_verified` are the real numbers, generated from the catalog by scripts/coverage.py and asserted by both test suites, so they cannot drift. Treat any gap between `encoded` and `estimated_total` as unexplored, not as work remaining.

field_notes.encoded: GENERATED. Contests from this sponsor currently in data/contests.seed.json.
field_notes.encoded_verified: GENERATED. Of those, how many carry verified:true -- rule read at the sponsor's own source.
field_notes.catalog_sponsors: Exact `sponsor` strings this org uses in the catalog. The join key. A sponsor string with no registry entry fails a test in both engines.
field_notes.status: complete | partial | blocked | not-started. `blocked` means a source problem that more effort will not fix -- read the note.

known_derived_sources.reason: Downstream aggregators. Useful only for locating a sponsor's primary domain.

region_map.$comment: Maps a contest record's `country` to the region used in coverage.by_region. Both engines read this rather than hard-coding a mapping. A country in the catalog that is missing here fails a test.

$region_map_note: OC is not an ISO country code. It is the code for a contest whose sponsor is a multi-national body inside one region -- currently only the Oceania DX Contest Committee, a joint VK/ZL committee. INTL is the same idea a level up, for a sponsor with no region at all. Neither is a country, and neither should be used where a national society owns the contest.

coverage.$comment: GENERATED by scripts/coverage.py from data/contests.seed.json. Do not hand-edit -- both test suites recompute it and fail on any drift, which is the point: this is the one block in the file that cannot go stale.

thin.$comment: Where the catalog is not a world calendar yet. `regions_with_nothing` is the headline: a region with zero contests is invisible to every operator in it, which is a worse failure than an unverified record.

engine_gaps.detail: CWops CWT runs weekly; SKCC Sprint, ARS Spartan Sprint, 4SQRP Second Sunday Sprint and NCCC Sprint run monthly. The old engine produced at most one occurrence per contest per year.
engine_gaps.fix: DONE. Rule types `weekly` and `monthly_nth_weekday` added and expand() returns a list. These high-frequency contests are now a large share of the catalog's 648 occurrences for 2026.

engine_gaps.detail: ARRL 10 GHz has two rounds; Stew Perry runs three or four times a year; EME has multiple weekends.
engine_gaps.fix: Currently handled by separate records per leg, which works but duplicates metadata. Consider a 'legs' array on one record.

engine_gaps.detail: ARRL EME dates are set annually based on lunar conditions and have no fixed rule. NCJ publishes Sprint dates without a recurrence rule, and CQ publishes dates for all eight of its contests without one.
engine_gaps.fix: DONE. Rule type `manual` takes an explicit date table. Note the CQ case is different and did NOT need it: CQ publishes no rule, but its published dates fit a stable recurrence, which is derivable and testable against eleven years of them. Prefer that over `manual` where the dates actually do follow a rule. The clearest instance found since is RAC Canada Winter (added 2026-08-17): eight dates from eight of RAC's own annual rules PDFs land on the fourth, third, third, third, fifth, third and fourth December Saturday -- and in 2026 on a Sunday. No ordinal fits, so 2027 onward is simply absent from the calendar rather than guessed, which is what `manual` is for.

engine_gaps.gap: Contests dated relative to a weekday near a fixed date
engine_gaps.detail: The WIA Remembrance Day Contest runs on the 'weekend in August closest to the 15th' -- neither an ordinal weekday nor a fixed date, and the two readings diverge every year the 15th is not itself a Saturday.
engine_gaps.fix: DONE. Rule type `nearest_weekday` takes a month, a day and a weekday, and moves at most three days in whichever direction is shorter. It can never be ambiguous: a tie would need a distance of 3.5 days, which does not exist because seven is odd. All seven cases are pinned by test in both engines, against WIA's published 2023 (August 12) and 2026 (August 15) dates.

engine_gaps.gap: Weekly contests that run only in some months
engine_gaps.detail: NZART's ZL Autumn and Winter Sprints run 'each Tuesday in April and August' and on no other Tuesday. `weekly` covered the whole year and `composite` was the obvious workaround.
engine_gaps.fix: DONE. `weekly` now takes the same optional `months` key `monthly_nth_weekday` already had. The composite workaround was tried first and rejected: it would have to name a fifth Tuesday, neither April nor August 2026 has one, and the sub-call raises rather than returning nothing -- so the whole contest would have vanished that year.

engine_gaps.detail: The old `local_time` flag conflated two opposite problems. Sponsor-anchored contests (4SQRP SSS, ARS Spartan Sprint) have exactly one correct UTC instant that moves an hour with DST; operator-anchored contests have none at all. This entry's own example was also wrong: ARRL moved 10 GHz off local time to fixed UTC and says so in the rules.
engine_gaps.fix: DONE. `local_time` retired. Sponsor-anchored records carry an IANA `timezone` plus `wall_clock` time specs, resolved through stdlib `zoneinfo`. Operator-anchored records carry `local_rolling` and expose no UTC instant at all (start/end are None). Both DST edges pinned by test. Windows needs `tzdata`; see requirements.txt. NOTE: no catalog record is operator-anchored today -- the capability is tested against a synthetic definition so the next one found does not get a fabricated instant.

estimated_scope.$comment: Pre-research estimates, kept for planning only. Compare against `coverage`, which is generated. See counts_are_estimates.
estimated_scope.note: Reaching WA7BNM's ~500 requires the long tail of small regional and weekly events, which is where the remaining effort compounds. 309 well-sourced contests covers essentially everything an active contester would ever enter. Two of these estimates are known to be unreachable as written: QRP ARCI's 8 are blocked at source and SARL's 10 are behind a dead host, so ~18 of the 309 need a human before they need an engineer.
